title: Storage round-trip covers put/get/delete/list on both SQL and KV backends
asA: developer configuring the storage backend on a new SingleCellObject
iWant: the shipped storage driver to round-trip put, get, delete and list on both the SQL and KV backends via a fixture switch
soThat: the applied project can elicit the backend at apply time (ADR-3403) and the shipped code path exercises both branches without code changes

acceptanceCriteria.description: A storage driver factory created with {backend: "sql"} and a storage driver factory created with {backend: "kv"} both round-trip put("k","v")->get("k")==="v", delete("k") followed by get("k")===undefined, and list({prefix:"p/"}) returns a Map keyed by the prefix. The driver.backend property reports the chosen backend on each factory.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two storage drivers, one on each backend
acceptanceCriteria.when: put/get/delete/list operations are driven on each driver in turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: both round-trip identically and driver.backend reports "sql" and "kv" respectively

acceptanceCriteria.description: F-6 SQL-specific: a storage driver with {backend:"sql"} exposes a .query(sql, ...args) verb that runs a typed SQL statement against the DO SQLite backend; a driver with {backend:"kv"} has no .query verb (typeof driver.query === "undefined"). This aligns with the ADR-3403 backend-swap contract: SQL supports typed columns and query, KV is put/get/delete/list only.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two storage drivers, one with backend "sql" and one with backend "kv"
acceptanceCriteria.when: the .query property is inspected on each driver
acceptanceCriteria.then: the SQL driver exposes .query as a function; the KV driver has no .query property

acceptanceCriteria.description: F-6 KV-specific: a storage driver with {backend:"kv"} refuses a batch-write call driver.batch([...]) with a named error kind DO_STORAGE_UNSUPPORTED_ON_KV naming the operation. A driver with {backend:"sql"} accepts driver.batch([...]) and returns the batched writes. The refusal is a first-class boundary of the KV backend rather than a silent unavailability.

F-7 write failure boundary: a driver.put("k","v") whose underlying backing store throws (simulated by a stubbed backing that rejects on put) surfaces the error unwrapped to the caller with a stable error kind DO_STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED whose message includes the key "k". No partial write persists (a subsequent get("k") returns undefined). The write-failed event does not land on the DO event sink because the storage layer is under the single-cell, not the facade.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a storage driver whose backing store put rejects synthetically
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call rejects with DO_STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED naming "k"; a subsequent get returns undefined

acceptanceCriteria.description: Empty and maximal collection boundaries: driver.list({prefix:""}) on an empty store returns an empty Map (size 0); driver.list({prefix:""}) on a store with 100 keys returns a Map of size 100 with every key preserved. The list result is a Map, not an array, so key insertion order does not affect the assertion.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a storage driver on an empty store and, separately, on a store with 100 keys
acceptanceCriteria.then: the empty store returns a Map of size 0; the populated store returns a Map of size 100

acceptanceCriteria.description: Value-size boundary (vendor-cited): a put("k", value) with value at 131072 bytes (the documented Cloudflare DO storage per-value cap of 128 KiB) succeeds and round-trips through get; a put("k", value) with value at 131073 bytes refuses with DO_STORAGE_VALUE_TOO_LARGE naming the observed byte count and the vendor limit URL. On the KV backend the equivalent cap is 25 MiB per the Workers KV limit page; the driver reports the cap it enforces.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a storage driver on the SQL backend with a 131072-byte value and, separately, a 131073-byte value
acceptanceCriteria.then: the 128 KiB value round-trips; the 131073-byte value refuses with DO_STORAGE_VALUE_TOO_LARGE naming the cap
